column5: _owned docstring still says "A sheaf that is its owner's alone"; change to "rectoverso".
Comment still says "James on his sheaf"; change to "rectoverso".

_render_entry calls self._refreshed(e) outside any try (live.refresh can raise on a render failure); whether render() should swallow it like the tick paths (core.py:1593,1664 via _rebuild_failed) is a behaviour decision, and the double `changed` with a settings rebuild is still there.

_pulling is still a set (expect_pull add, end_pull discard) and Commits._pull calls self._pulling at commits.py:674 before _repo_lock; make it a per-address count (increment/decrement) so an overlapping pull does not clear the other's window.
Hub.pulled has no per-file guard, so a raise from _page_of leaves later files in _pulling; wrap each file in try/finally (or try/except calling end_pull(address, None)) and do the same in pulling().

First half is FIXED (create clears expectation at mcp.py:1174, update at mcp.py:1254); second half holds: `not is_pull and not is_own` short-circuits so a pending _own entry survives a pull; evaluate is_own first, then is_pull.
drop() now compares os.path.realpath(folder) with os.path.realpath(root.path).

drop() still runs forget_root then os.rmdir/write_json unguarded, and mcp.py:1038 calls it inside `except BaseException` so an OSError replaces the refusal; catch OSError around the drop call (or inside drop) and rmdir before forget_root.
_loose reads raw args["doc"] and tests bare before _named strips it; use doc = _named(args["doc"]) at the top of _loose.
Non-bare doc refuses only a true keep (`if args.get("keep")`), keep=false passes.
The create path calls writes.told(address) in its except BaseException after expect_own (mcp.py:1165), so a refused create leaves no stale hash.
Titles.read still does `self._kept[key] = ...` then `return self._kept[key]` after a possible clear() by another thread; compute value into a local, store it, return the local.
hub.writes.last and last_way_back are still two separate lock takes; add one WriteLog method returning both under one lock (cosmetic).
The Sheaf wrapper still gets class `sheaf-list sheaf-sheaf`; reuse of list.css looks deliberate, so add a comment saying so (no behaviour change).
Not a defect: a cost remark, and Titles caches by (path, mtime, size) (sheaf_view.py:36-44) as the finding itself says.
_with_default has an `empty` regex that fills an empty `tiroir = ""` line in place and then verifies with tomllib, so no second key is written.
connect() runs check_config(origin) before store.set and add_mcp_entry, converting ConfigError to ConnectError "Nothing was written."
add_mcp_entry still reads and os.replaces ~/.claude.json with no lock; Claude Code takes no lock to coordinate with, so any fix (retry on mtime change, re-read before replace) is a decision.

probe still does r.read(1 << 20) with a per-socket-operation timeout, so an event-stream answer kept open with keep-alives holds the command; a fix needs a decision on an overall deadline or reading only to the first data: line.
of() still filters `not r.invalid`, so an invalid laptop row cannot be revoked through /_/laptops/revoke; whether invalid rows should be listed and revocable is a product decision.
signed_names skips a laptop row when cfg is None, so loopback mode no longer counts a laptop token as signed by Claude Code.
The `if address in self.hub.writes._own:` guard reading a private attribute is still there before told(); drop the guard and call told(address) alone.

Same drop() as item 20: forget_root runs before os.rmdir(folder), so a folder that is a symlink raises NotADirectoryError after the root is forgotten; fix together with item 20 (rmdir first, catch OSError).
_check enforces schema type boolean for every call (`keep must be true or false`), so keep="false" is refused for a bare doc too.
About the PR #389 description text, not code on main; nothing to change in the repo.

way_back returns None for a non-plain session id before the ownership check, dropping another member's valid Remote Control link; fall through to the remote branch instead (and fix the docstring clause "an id that is not a plain id" to match SPEC 8.6).
window.open still runs in the fetch rejection handler (after the async ask); a hang-proof fix needs an AbortController timeout on ask(), whose length is a decision.
Members are now "Alice Example", "Carol Example", "Bob Example", "Dave Example"; no real surnames remain in the config text.
Docstring still names "agency-tiroir's stage sheaf-agents-hub-2026-11-07" and "read off the box's tokens.json"; rewrite without them.
Docstring still says "only Alice may override it"; reword to "only the operator may override it".

wayBackWhere.say is still `say(t, true)` (red 7 s error toast + incident) for the informational Remote Control message; give where.say an info flag (second argument from sheaf.js:84) and pass false for that message.
SPEC item 11 still does not state that a member page loaded without sheaf.js shows the session name as plain text (page.js comment at 137 says it); add one sentence.

_share still builds the edit from e.live.current()[1] after the place.held block ends and sends `after` as the hash; capture the text whose hash is `after` inside change (the with_share_line result, or text) and compute share_edit from it.

may_open still does not ask shared_with/member_owns (only visible-style fm checks plus opened_by_line); the save guard's under-lock recheck on a loose page needs a decision on what it must judge, and it is trust-boundary code.
_told_text still uses text.replace(real, told) over the whole text; replace only whole-address occurrences (regex with a non-path-character boundary) (cosmetic).
owner_of reads through _registry(), which a listing holds once via remembered() (loose.py:~180), so loose.json is read once per listing; only the cheap realpath per folder remains.
A deploy-ordering note (ship the mod and library door pass-through with this deploy), not a code defect on main.
retargets() still drops agent:<token> equal to targetNow(); whether a laptop's own token should be offered as a Retarget target is a product decision.
_retarget still calls targets.restore outside _reading after start_member_tell is refused; moving it under the lock touches the lock order, so it needs a decision.
entry_name still maps https://[::1]:8443 to sheaf---1-8443; renaming changes the key of existing MCP entries in users' ~/.claude.json, so it needs a decision.
tiroir_of still reads .sheaf.toml of the file own folder only (load_root_config documents "never from a subfolder"); using the registered root needs a decision on how a laptop finds the root.
keep_row is still read_state, set, write_state with no lock; take a file lock around the read-modify-write.
Door.tool now checks content[0] and text, but got["doc"], got["hash"] (send.py:423,434,594) are still read unchecked from the parsed JSON; validate the result shape in tool() and raise SendError.
_leave_theirs still write_text_atomic over FILE.tiroir.md with no check; whether to refuse, number it or overwrite is a decision.
cmd_pull hashes the local text before the door call and writes at line 631 without re-reading; re-read and compare md_hash just before write_text_atomic.
library-door#241 is still there (SPEC.md:969 says acme/library-door#241); replace with a resolvable reference or plain wording.
The branch tests isinstance(reason, ssl.SSLError), so SSLEOFError and resets count as untrusted; narrow to ssl.SSLCertVerificationError and apply it to a bare SSLError from read() too.
Recovery text still promises "exists already, and it is this one" but _create (send.py:418-420) answers "was not sent from this file. Rename"; reword the guidance to what the rerun prints.
Concerns the PR description only; SPEC.md:1709 says "5 s each" and the code comment says the messages before a call, so nothing in the repo is wrong.
_read still returns {} on an unparseable reports.json and the next _write replaces it; refuse versus quarantine-and-reset is a decision.
repo not in self._queues is still read outside self._guard at lines 700 and 728; take the guard for the membership test only (not across provider.token).
self._hosts is still written unlocked and never expires; the expiry policy is a decision.
hub.repos is now wired (repos_mod.from_config); the remaining round trip is the intended SPEC behaviour, not a defect.
_origin_of_server still reads only top-level mcpServers of ~/.claude.json; supporting project scope changes which entries the mod trusts.
followSession is gone from core.ts, but Poller.session (core.ts:32,41) is still set in arm() and read nowhere; remove the dead field.
leave() still does not clear p.delivered; clearing could change repeat-Tell behaviour across /clear, so it needs a decision.
Intended and documented behaviour ("a command name wins over a file of that name: ./name opens the file"), no defect.
session.start still calls restore(m.p, ...) whatever p.armedFor is; guarding it changes resume semantics.
undo = putBack still runs after a drop at turn end and leaves p.stored out of step; whether a dropped Tell resubmits is a decision.
turn.start still ignores a Tell whose text lacks t.message; errs toward a repeat as documented, any change depends on runtime behaviour.
may_open still calls opened_by_line(member, address) with text=None (re-reads the file); passing the locked text means changing its six callers.
visible() still re-reads and parses via opened_by_line for each refused page with no _front cache; needs a caching design.
shared_with still uses audience() with no private-source check unlike opened_by_line (core.py:1398); access rule change in security code.
Unticking a Share line is refused by the Counter difference while the message says "add or change"; reword the message to include unticking.
The agency-short check accepts a short starting with . or - that visibility._BOX_RE/_NAMES_RE cannot parse; require a short matching [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* in that check.
The OPTIONAL_TABLE_KEYS filtered dict is still built twice (lines 393 and 395); add a small helper.
_folder still refuses "" through loose.folder_path, so a page cannot move to the root top; allowing it is a product decision.
Versions.rename (line 275) and _Store.rename (line 345) still return without touching new when old is absent; drop the stale new entry first.
self.hub.file(new).read_text is still outside any try; catch OSError/NotFound and raise a ToolError.
before = os.lstat(src) is still outside the try and a FileNotFoundError is not mapped by handler.py:1574; move it inside or catch it and raise KeyError.
forget_root still takes only self._lock, not moves._LOCK, so _undo can restore forgotten Forwards; lock-order change is risky.
_cache_good (introduced for _git_version) caches only a non-None read and retries after RETRY_READ_EVERY=60 s.

On git below 2.44 commit_known is still False for every ok report so sheaf prints "is it pushed?"; the hub now logs once at start (repos.py:215); fixing the message needs a protocol change (None for look-off).
root_config still forces commit/push on any root with clone set while Hub.clone_of returns "" when repos is None; gating or refusing is a decision.
decide() without a token still reads origin/HEAD:.sheaf.toml with look=True and can cache read-only; fails safe, the fix is a design choice.

In _update, _reply and _move the address comes from _address, which judges visibility first (mcp.py:422-438); _created checks root ownership before _writable (mcp.py:1052-1059), so the read-only line is not shown to a caller who cannot see the page.
read_only_line still returns self._why.get(repo) without checking it was set for the current branch; store the branch with the reason and ignore a mismatch.
The check still compares owner keys only; SPEC.md:997 says against every other short and id; matching the spec could stop the start of existing configs.
owner_of matching on owner_key (short, else id) is the SPEC.md:997 behaviour, as the finding itself says; not a defect.
restore_trash now uses os.link (no replace) under file_lock(dest) and loose-keep.lock, with a Taken check (commit c10c4f69).
_sweep_root now reads Marks and stamps ARCHIVED in one hold of loose-keep.lock.
_sleep_one still overwrites "restore" with the current (shrunk) listing; keep an existing non-empty restore.
purge still os.scandir()s root/.sheaf/trash without the _plain_dir lstat check, so a symlinked .sheaf or trash is followed; call _plain_dir on .sheaf and trash first.
marks_of still applies the owner archived marks to rows shared with other members; whether recipients should see their own view is a product decision.
seen.json/archived.json are still pruned only by trash(); pruning in the sweep needs a rule for pages the listing omits.
Lock still held across the `git --version` read in _cache_good; the finding itself says it is bounded and not a defect, so add one sentence to the docstring saying so.
The "said once, at the hub's start" comment is true per Repos() construction only; reword the comment to "at each Repos construction (one per hub)".
The start-message tests monkeypatch _git_version; add a test with a failing then working real read at Repos() start asserting the recovery line is printed.
Reply now renders the reply's text field (esc(r.text)); fixed by commit 9d49bd10 "Team tab: a reply shows its text".
_with_team op "page" still calls json.loads(m.group(2)) with no try; wrap in try/except ValueError and return the body unchanged as the doc/mount branch does.
Team comments are still keyed by the address and nothing renames them on a Move or Forward; following Forwards or re-keying on move is a design decision.

Write log lines on disk are now retracted (writes.undo appends a retracted line, writelog.py:243), but hub.wrote/committed index entry, the git commit and made loose folders are still not undone in the rollback; undoing a commit in a git root is a decision.
hub.versions.put/forget still used unconditionally; use (hub._versions_of(root) or hub.versions) as outgoing.py:100 does, for put and forget.
transfers.json is still keyed by b["id"] alone with no peer; keying by (peer, id) changes the stored format and the local-caller case, so it needs a decision.
owner_for still runs before transfers.lock and the id lookup; move the recorded-answer lookup first (or owner_for inside the lock after it).
carry still writes the transfer line with the sender-supplied `by` (only clean()ed); whether to use the owner's name or the peer origin instead is a decision.
handler.py:1496 still has holds_loose or visible, and Archive.trash lstats only the last component of src; add a realpath containment check of src inside root.path in trash().
A FileNotFoundError/NotFound for a page already gone is still answered 404 via _page_gone without record_exception; recording it vs keeping diagnostics quiet is a decision.
The unlink after os.link is now guarded: except OSError calls _drop(dest) and raises loose.Refused (409), so the page is not left at both places.
restore_trash still uses os.link and answers 409 on a filesystem without hard links; adding a fallback (renameat2 NOREPLACE or copy+fsync) is a decision.
The name branch of _add checks only `name in self._roots`, not RESERVED; refuse name.casefold()==RESERVED there (a root registered earlier as Clients is not covered).
adopt still keeps the client's rd-edit-meta block verbatim; filtering it to known keys is a security design decision.
The page script still survives only when byte-identical to this hub's page_script(); rewriting build fields for the page route or tolerating another build is a decision.
check_root still answers {"ready": True} while send_root (outgoing.py:271) counts only {"ok": True}; no caller exists for either yet, so which side changes is a decision for part 2.
send_root still calls answer.get on whatever post returned (None for an empty body, or a list); guard with isinstance(answer, dict) and hold the batch as "failed".
Moves.sent indexes row["sent"] and row["held"] (and hold row["held"] at :154) directly; use row.get(..., default) to survive an old or hand-edited row.
_root_shape still accepts an empty owner_email and duplicate paths; require a non-empty owner_email and a set of unique paths.
report.moved_to is still printed unfiltered; require .isprintable() on moved_to in the report check at send.py:310.

signals.send_group (src/sheafmd/signals.py:92) takes only a Popen child that leads its own group and refuses anything else, so a group signal to a process the test did not start cannot be sent; no killpg guard is needed.
The spin loop is replaced by wait_until_ended(done.pid), which has a deadline.
is_ending still waits up to EXEC_WINDOW for a live process whose environ cannot be read; telling unreadable from empty is a change of the guard's rule.
post now opens through connect._NO_REDIRECT, so the bearer is not sent to a redirect target (commit 9921afbf).
undo and restore append a `retracted` line and the kept lines to the file, so a restart does not bring the carried lines back (commits 9921afbf, 2b0db61e).
_unkeep and _unarchive still share one contextlib.suppress; give each its own suppress so a failed _unkeep does not skip _unarchive.
The sender's timeout is still urllib's per-socket-operation timeout; a total-deadline call is a design change.
The unreaped test still asserts nothing after the wait; add assert proc_state(done.pid) == "zombie" before done.wait.
_sweep_root still lists pages outside any lock and does not take moves._LOCK; adding it changes the hub's lock order for the sweep, a decision.
_own_loose still runs under moves._LOCK (also in _delete); the finding calls it a throughput cost only, so add a comment stating the cost is accepted.
The assert right after the first Delete click still has no wait; add a short until-stable check that no POST went out.
_store._change still leaves self._data changed in memory when write_json raises; reload self._data from the file in an except branch before re-raising.
The comment now says "a Forward that cannot be written is a row in the diagnostics log" and does not claim OSError, so the broad except Exception matches its comment.
The way-back refusal adds install unconditionally from repos.install_url; add it only when non-empty, as incoming.py:275 does.
refusal() still calls provider.token and report() calls it again (repos.py:701) for a repo with no clone; sharing one token per request needs a design.
The docstring still has a run of spaces after "its Forward);"; replace with one space.

In Hub.renamed the _page_of/Address.parse calls (1744-1747) and the admit/tell_live block (1753-1755) are outside the try at 1760; move them inside (or wrap the pair) so a failure is one move-store-failed row for that pair, not write-log-failed via Commits._tell (commits.py:739).

place.held(a), place.held(b) is old-then-new while SPEC 1140 and lockorder.py:9 say ascending; safe because moves.exclusive() is held (same at moves.py:109); reword the SPEC/lockorder sentence to say the order inside the moves lock is free.
Observation that the test asserts only the spy filter on a non-clone dir, which is what its docstring says it tests (which Repos made the look); no defect.

Observation, no defect: the test's job is that the made-up SENDER_PID (tests/test_hub_lifecycle.py:234) stays above 2**22 against a faked cmdline; the kernel limit is stated in the comment at :233 and cannot be proved by a test.
Still a bare hub.commits.settle() (also 110, 112, 124, 136, 144); settle returns False on timeout (commits.py:868); prefix with `assert`.

An old page without CFG.branch sends no branch and handler._read_on (handler.py:1257-1262) answers 400 for a clone page; tolerating a missing branch would weaken the guard, so a transition path is a decision.
_save passes the branch guard into e.live.save, which answers an rid replay `again` before calling it, so the switch is hidden on a replay; showing it needs a decision on the answer shape.
Not a defect: catch_up's docstring (1656-1659) states a failed rebuild is tried again on the next request, and _rebuild_failed (core.py:1799ff) bounds the logging; the finding itself says no crash.
A_FUNCTION still accepts `(` followed by anything; anchor it as r"^\s*(async\s*)?(\(.*?\)\s*=>|[\w$]+\s*=>|function\b)".
PAGE_TESTS.glob("*.py") is top level only; tests/page has no subfolder today, so no gap now; use rglob.
wake() calls _use (sleeping=False, writes clones.json) before _restore at :417; move _use after a successful _restore (keep it for the nothing-out return) so a failed widen leaves the row asleep.
provider.token(repo) runs inside `with self.holding(dest)` (:408); fetching it outside the lock needs the sleeping/restore check redone after, a lock-order and race decision.
Every wake() takes the repo's commit lock and _use rewrites clones.json even for an awake clone; throttling last_used changes the sleep clock's accuracy, a decision.
sleep_moved updates an already-sleeping row under _records only, not holding(dest), as wake does (:408); taking the repo lock there changes the lock order with the sleep threads.

roots.lookup matches only on realpath (roots.py:408, _find compares r.path to a realpath'd folder) and roots are stored realpath'd (roots.py:321), so root.path is already resolved when relative_to runs at core.py:383.
WriteLog.drop has no caller in src/ or tests/ (git grep `drop(` finds only unrelated drops); delete it, or add a test, and fix the RETRACTED comment at :21.
restore writes `replace(line, address=address)` to the file but keeps `deque(kept, ...)` with the old addresses in memory; build the deque from the replaced lines, as undo does at :256.
restore re-appends up to KEEP lines plus a marker per failed landing; bounded by rotation and lossless, so any change (diffing the lines) is a design decision.
use_peer_file now wraps mkdir/os.open/replace in `except OSError` and raises ConnectError("cannot keep the token in ... nothing was written").
`peer add` still prints `sheaf peer use <address> <token>` although the `use` help (cli.py:1093-1096) calls a token argument discouraged; print the stdin form (token piped on the standard input).
peer_credential_name still maps every non [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '-', so a:8443 and a-8443 share a file; a different encoding renames credential files already deployed, a decision.
mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True) leaves an existing folder's mode; chmod-ing a folder the user named is a decision (the file is 0600 either way).
Both except branches (OSError :146, BaseException :149) unlink the temp when `made`, so no .new token is left after a failed os.replace.
_WARNED (:78) records the file name; the warning prints only when the name is not yet in it, once per process.

Submit sends to /_/move-folder even when input.value.trim() === at, and moves.py:189 answers 409 "A folder cannot be moved into itself."; in the submit handler, form.remove() and return when the value is unchanged.
A refusal goes to the shared say() line (:355), not beside the form; where to show it (per-form line) is a UI decision.
`made = True` follows os.open at :134-135; a one-statement window only a KeyboardInterrupt reaches and no code change closes it fully; accept or restructure with a decision.
os.close(fd) in the finally can replace the write/fsync error with close's; catch OSError around the close when an exception is already propagating.

Door._asleep returns None for an unbound token (member None), as the SPEC 13 comment in core.wake_for_write says the front matter of a sleeping page cannot be read, so whether it is `visibility: project` is unknown; giving it the asleep line is a policy decision.
tracked() decodes with errors="replace" (:107); decode with surrogateescape (os.fsdecode) so a non-UTF-8 name resolves to its real file.
Docstring says a hit is never the matched text, but a name in a path prints in `path:0 term N` (add(path, 0, key) at :122); reword the docstring and SPEC row to say the path is printed.
The guard's own files skip every address of every ALLOW entry (`key in {k for _, k in allow}`), documented as intended; narrowing it to one entry per file is a policy change.

For a list/Sheaf page, create() runs before the stylesheet wait and `page` stays assigned when stale() returns at :454; unmounting it there changes the mount lifecycle shared by the overtaking draw, needs a decision.
Comment cites a specific test by name (test_rename_folder_onto_a_taken_name...) and `9 of 240 runs`; reword without the test name so a rename cannot stale it.
Still unguarded on main: wrap t.start() so a failure discards the thread from _threads and the repo from _queues, then re-raises.
Still rests on helper[0].join(0.5); making the red/green signal deterministic needs a different test design (e.g. an event the patched start waits on).
catch path in teamAct never sets teamAsk = null (only the success path at 3105 does); reset it in the catch.
`if (teamBusy) return;` still drops every Team-tab click silently; whether to say something or queue is a UX decision.
`if (!text) return;` still silent; add a say(...) line (wording is the only choice).
LEAVING_JS still clears __leaving when defaultPrevented/returnValue is set, and page.js:4190 does set both on unload with unsaved edits; fix needs a browser run to settle.
tab fixture still ends in landed() -> settled() which waits for #rd-menu-btn; no current test leaves for a non-sheaf page, so a hypothetical; changing it needs browser tests.
landed()/settled() still see only a reload that has begun; acknowledged follow-up needing a browser-side design.
A CI flake record of a test the PR did not touch; already filed as tickets 137 and 141, nothing to fix here.
Test still uses slow versions.put so _in_time (incoming.py:140) trips before hub.writes.carry (incoming.py:143), so undo returns early; reaching undo needs a different failure point, a test redesign.
Docstring still says "as a `Landing`"; the object is `_Own` (line 62).
undo still subtracts every line in own.lines; filter by address (no behaviour change, states intent).
`import contextlib` still sits after `import os`.
Still depends on the sleep child being under EXEC_WINDOW old at the second read; making it deterministic needs a test redesign.
carries_this_run still waits only within EXEC_WINDOW of process start; pre-existing, accepted limit: add a one-line comment saying so.
The finding is about the PR description on GitHub, not a repo file; nothing to change on main.
Coupling is real and uncommented at the src call sites (await link.onload before create; takeAgent before #rd-menu); add a comment at each.
d.state = state still runs before _end, so the delivered clear is duplicated (was == "delivered" at 129 and _end at 149); set the state after _end or drop it.
_watch_drops still runs expire() before _read_drop_statuses(), so a reply ends the drop first; the finding itself says harmless, ordering change would be a design call.
A note that the author did not run the test locally; not a defect in code.
Still `if (gone || lpanel.hidden) return;` on the POST success path, so the made line is dropped when the panel is closed meanwhile; what to show (token is shown once) is a decision.
Network-failure handler still says() without checking lpanel.hidden; add `|| lpanel.hidden` as in the success path.
Copy button text is set to "Copied" and nothing resets it; reset in laptopMake/laptopsClose.
EMOJI_ATTR_RE still matches any <span>; narrow the comment (and the one at 825) to say it strips data-emoji from any span.
keys() then join still not atomic; the cap is soft by a few: say so in a comment next to SHARED_MAX (line 882).
Shared.join still drops a sub silently when closed and _live_join answers 200; telling the page needs a protocol choice.
The _stream loop still never checks sub.closed, so a replaced Shared (old.close()) idles until the peer closes; return when the subscription is closed.
_live_leave still calls _shared_of only when key is a string, so a non-string key answers 200; call _shared_of first.
Every lock winner still opens the shared stream (lock() at 219-229) regardless of any page asking; lazy-open is a design change.
About the PR description on GitHub, not a repo file; the finding itself says the merged files add no private names.
The finding states it probed dl, details, div, sup, link text, br and found no failing case; no defect.
`sc !== box` still present and dead (an <input> cannot contain cont); remove it.
TASK_LISTS ids "ordered"/"ordered from three" still name task lists though gfm renders `1. [ ]` as plain text; rename the ids or comment.

check still requires _render_source of the block but box_number None (flipped render fails) drops the action; falling back to line reading changes what counts as an action and the save guard, so it needs a decision.
Describes a one-time render cost per new text (cached by (content, at)); an observation, no defect to fix.

→ 137 item 4. _EMOJI_TOKEN is still replaced by `:name:` regardless of table depth, so a raw-HTML table saves <th>:+1:</th>; inside <table depth substitute the emoji glyph (as the pipe/slash loop at 768-776 does).
inlineButton words are still [label, a.word] where _word (the_list.py:397) maps legacy "Move to" to "Belongs to"; pass "Move to" as a third word.
Transient across the ticket 168 restart only (a page loaded before the deploy); the window has passed, no code to change.
Code now says Belongs to (the_list.py:65, MOVE_OLD only a legacy read at :66), so drop 'until ticket 168' and reword 'a Move to is a one-off too' to Belongs to.
_styled_marks has no heading check (parents test only em/strong); skip when span has an h1-h6 parent.
